title: Truck Accident Guide for San Diego
metaDescription: San Diego truck accident guide: commercial carrier claims, Pure comparative fault rules, and evidence preservation.
excerpt: Educational San Diego, CA guide — 2-year SOL, local hospitals, and insurer tactics. Not legal advice.

sections.heading: First 10 minutes: safety and 911
paragraphs: A collision on I-95 or surface streets in San Diego can escalate quickly. If vehicles are drivable and it is safe, move to a shoulder or parking lot. Turn on hazard lights.
Call 911 when anyone reports pain, airbags deploy, fluids leak, or traffic is blocked. San Diego County dispatch will route San Diego police or state patrol depending on location.
list: Stay inside the vehicle with seatbelts on if traffic passes closely at highway speed
Do not admit fault — describe facts only
Request a crash report number before officers leave

sections.heading: San Diego documentation checklist
paragraphs: Photograph all vehicles, license plates, VIN stickers, skid marks, traffic signals, and visible injuries. San Diego insurers expect timestamped photos.
Collect names and phone numbers from witnesses — independent accounts matter on I-95, I-75, US-1 and in San Diego County.
Exchange insurance policy numbers and registration; note employer if the other driver was working.

sections.heading: Medical care within 24 hours
paragraphs: San Diego has San Diego Regional Medical Center and San Diego General Hospital among its major facilities. Level I trauma care is available at San Diego Level I Trauma Center.
Whiplash, concussion, and internal injuries may appear hours later. A same-day urgent care or ER visit creates a medical record insurers cannot easily dismiss.

sections.heading: California reporting rules
paragraphs: California requires crash reporting when injuries, death, or significant property damage occur. Minimum liability limits are 30/60/15.
Cooperate with officers; request a copy of the report through the investigating agency. If police do not respond, check https://dot.ca.gov/ for self-report thresholds.

sections.heading: Insurance notification without hurting your claim
paragraphs: Notify your carrier with basic facts — date, location, vehicles involved. Decline recorded statements until you understand your coverage and injuries.
California uses Pure comparative comparative negligence; anything you say can affect fault allocation.

sections.heading: Evidence preservation in San Diego
paragraphs: Dashcam, Ring doorbell, and business security footage near San Diego downtown interchange is often deleted within 7–30 days. Send written preservation letters when appropriate.
Save repair estimates, rental receipts, and mileage to medical appointments.

sections.heading: When to explore attorney matching
paragraphs: Consider a free consultation if you were hospitalized, fault is disputed, a commercial vehicle was involved, or the adjuster offers a quick settlement before treatment finishes.

faq.question: Is this legal advice for my San Diego case?
faq.answer: No. This is general education from WreckMatch LLC, a referral service — not a law firm. Consult a licensed attorney for advice about your situation.

faq.question: What is the statute of limitations in California?
faq.answer: Most injury claims face a 2-year deadline, but exceptions apply. Verify your dates with counsel.
